notes: context-fog-of-war bundle mapping for a live round folder (.sdlc/evals/rounds/<date>-<slug>/), T-0248, revised T-0259. One dev proxy trace line (traces/<day>.jsonl, T-0151) is one model_request, plus (when it carries `events`) one retrieval event and one tool_result event per non-terminal tool result. conversationId is the line's runId: the id a probe sent as the x-a2ui-run-id header (run-id.ts), so a round imports as one conversation per probe run. A line with no runId (a turn from the dev UI, or any round archived before T-0259, which use fog-manifest-v1.json) is excluded with a missing-conversation-id warning, never grouped by guess. requestId is the line's `at` ISO time, unique per line in every committed round; it identifies the turn, it is not a causal join, and the retrieval and tool_result events target it explicitly (targetRequestId). The `events` block is written at two independent points. retrieval.chunkIds are the exemplar ids deps.retrieve returned (produce.ts); includedChunkIds are framedExemplarIds, the ids the prompt composer emitted a block for (system-prompt.ts fewShot), so an exemplar retrieved but not framed is a retrieved-not-submitted finding. retrieval.success is false when retrieval returned nothing, so an empty shard is excluded, not counted as a checked pair. tool_result events are the results the provider adapter had in hand (anthropic.ts tool loop, non-terminal calls only: render_surface is terminal and has no continuation by design); toolResultIds are the ids it placed in the next upstream request, so a result never submitted is a tool-result-not-propagated finding. A turn with no integration tool has no tool_result event, so that detector has no eligible pair on it. complete is events.complete, written true only when the turn reached its final meta-line, so a turn that threw or halted midway declares no completeness and its pairs report a gap, never a finding. Referenced resources fetched versus listed are already in routing.references (load full or index-only, ids and kinds); they stay unmapped because the proxy sees them only as the user message text, one side of any pair. Not mappable in this vocabulary (kept as hashed artifacts): runs/*/report.json and fixture.json (they join to a trace line by `<day>.jsonl:<line>`, which no canonical event type can target), the routing block of T-0239 and later lines (sections and mini-skills are object lists), and retries and failure codes (no canonical event). T-0311: each trace round is also one model_request (rule 4), keyed by the round's own requestId (`<at>#<round>`; the round repeats the line's runId because a round is read on its own), with attempt the round ordinal; it carries the request's maxTokens, the round's outputTokens (summed over the round's upstream requests; render_surface is terminal, so a capture round is one request) and the stopReason of the round's last request, the fields the stop-at-cap detector reads. The line-level model_request keeps the turn's context ids and carries no token counts, so that detector skips it. The prompt text behind routing.sections[].digest and rounds[].userDigest sits in the dev proxy's .agent-traces/prompts/<digest>.txt, local and git-ignored; run-capped.ts does not archive it into a round folder, and it is not mapped.
